page: Microsoft Azure NC288ds_xl_RTXPRO6000BSE_v6 is a high-scale GPU-accelerated instance within the NCdsRTXPRO6000BSEv6XL series, managed under Microsoft Hyper-V. The platform is powered by an x86_64 Intel processor architecture, allocating 288 dedicated vCPUs and 1032 GB of system RAM, which provides 3.58 GB of memory per core. Hardware acceleration is driven by two NVIDIA Blackwell RTX PRO 6000 GPUs supplying a combined 192 GB of video memory.

Data handling and transient storage requirements are supported by 15943 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, offering high sequential and random I/O throughput directly on the host. The instance is also Azure Premium Storage capable for durable managed disk attachments. Networking configurations should account for the absence of complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which must be provisioned separately if external reachability is required.

From an infrastructure perspective, this instance concentrates heavy computational, graphical, and storage resources onto a single footprint. This consolidation eliminates the network overhead typically associated with multi-node clustering for large workloads. The configuration is best matched to demanding enterprise tasks such as high-fidelity 3D rendering, computer-aided engineering, complex simulation, AI inference, and large-scale visual computing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure NC288ds_xl_RTXPRO6000BSE_v6 is a high-density GPU-accelerated virtual machine designed for compute and data-heavy visual computing and AI workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture using Intel processors managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 288 dedicated vCPUs alongside 1032 GB of system RAM, yielding 3.58 GB per core. Acceleration is delivered by two NVIDIA Blackwell RTX PRO 6000 GPUs offering 192 GB of combined VRAM. Local high-speed storage is bundled directly with 15943 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, supplemented by Premium Storage capability for external disks. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. Combining high-throughput parallel compute, substantial accelerator memory, and massive local I/O bandwidth, this configuration provides efficient resource density for large-scale graphics rendering, deep learning model execution, workstation visualization, and data-intensive simulation workflows.
